Hi Ana! Here's how the Get Clássica and the Get Smart compare, based on their user manuals.

**Main differences**
- **Mobile connection:** The Get Clássica comes with a 3G chip with a free data plan [14]. The Get Smart comes with a 4G chip with a free data plan [7].
- **Screen:** The Get Smart has a touchscreen [7].
- **Settings on the machine:** On the Get Smart, you tap "Configurar" on the home screen. From there you can manage Wi-Fi, 4G and Bluetooth, turn on data-saving mode, run a connection test, adjust screen brightness, set up Kiosk Mode and run hardware tests, including the camera and printing [2].
- **What's in the box:** The Get Clássica includes a charger, a USB cable, a 3G chip and two sustainable Getnet paper rolls [14]. The Get Smart includes a charger and a 4G chip [7].
- **Warranty and battery:** The Get Clássica manual lists a 1-year warranty from the date you sign up, or 3 months for the Renova Com Bobina model. It also says the battery can last between 4h and 8h, depending on use, screen brightness and signal [14]. The Get Smart information I have doesn't list its warranty or battery life.

**What they have in common**
- Both accept chip cards, magnetic stripe cards and contactless payments with cards, phones and digital wallets [7][13][15].
- Both accept Pix by QR Code or tap (NFC) [13][15]. For the Get Smart, you need to enable Pix in the Getnet Brasil app first [13].
- Both connect via Wi-Fi and Bluetooth [3][7].

I don't have pricing or plan details for either machine. If you'd like help choosing the right one for Padaria Sol Nascente, I can open a case with a human agent for you.

The Get Smart evidence [13] mentions digital wallets. The Get Clássica evidence [15] lists only "cartões, celular, smartwatch, etc." and never mentions digital wallets. The other claims are supported.

Hi Ana! Here's how receivables anticipation works at Getnet.

**What it is**
Anticipation lets you access, before the usual date, the money from credit card sales you've already made. It can help when installment sales are paid out over time and you need cash for suppliers, fixed expenses or a good buying opportunity [4].

**When a sale can be anticipated**
A sale becomes available for anticipation from D+1 (one business day after the sale) until D-3 (three business days before the amount would be credited to your account) [1]. For example:
- A sale made on 04/03 can be anticipated from 05/03.
- If the credit is due to land in your account on 03/04, the sale can be anticipated until 31/03 [1].

**How to request it**
If you're **not** a Santander account holder [2]:
- Automatic anticipation
- One-off ("eventual") anticipation through the Getnet Service Center
- Anticipation on your Getnet POS machine, done by you directly on the device

If you **are** a Santander account holder, you have the same options, plus [2]:
- Your account manager at a Santander branch
- Internet Banking (for business accounts, if that channel is enabled)

Santander account holders can also check upcoming credits in the Santander Portal under Consultas → Lançamentos Futuros → Todos os Movimentos [2].

The information I have doesn't include the rates or costs of anticipation for your business. If you'd like that, or help deciding whether it makes sense for the bakery, I can open a case with a Getnet human agent for you. Just let me know!
cases.judge_reason: all claims supported. The answer's description, D+1/D-3 windows and examples, request channels for Santander and non-Santander customers, and the Santander Portal path all match evidence [1], [2] and [4]. It states that rates are not in its information and offers a human-agent case, which the input allows. No other payment company is recommended.

Hola, Ana. Te explico cómo funciona la anticipación de ventas en Getnet:

**¿Qué es?**
Te permite recibir antes del plazo el dinero de las ventas que ya hiciste con tarjeta de crédito. Ayuda a mantener la caja equilibrada, por ejemplo para pagar proveedores o cubrir gastos fijos cuando las ventas en cuotas se van recibiendo con el tiempo [4].

**¿Qué ventas puedes anticipar?**
Las ventas con crédito, al contado o en cuotas [3].

**¿Cuándo está disponible?**
Una venta se puede anticipar desde D+1 (un día hábil después de la venta) hasta D-3 (tres días hábiles antes de que el valor se acredite en tu cuenta) [1]. Por ejemplo:
- Una venta hecha el 04/03 estará disponible para anticipar desde el 05/03.
- Si el crédito se acreditará en tu cuenta el 03/04, podrás anticiparla hasta el 31/03 [1].

**¿Cómo se hace?**
Directamente en la aplicación Getnet Brasil, disponible para Android e iOS, sin burocracia [3].

**Antes de anticipar, conviene revisar** [3]:
- La tasa de anticipación (el porcentaje por día o por mes).
- El plazo de los cobros: cuanto más lejana la fecha de pago, mayor suele ser el costo.
- El valor real que recibirás después de descontar la tasa.
- Si existe otra forma de cubrir esa necesidad con un costo menor.

La información que tengo no incluye las tasas aplicables a tu cuenta. Si quieres conocerlas, puedo abrir un caso con un agente humano de Getnet.
